reasoning: This is a single-arm neoadjuvant study of durvalumab + chemotherapy in triple-negative breast cancer. Step 1 (TARGET ENGAGEMENT): No direct PD-L1 engagement data provided, but durvalumab is a well-established PD-L1 inhibitor with known pharmacology. Step 2 (PATHWAY MODULATION): No biomarker data on immune activation or T-cell responses reported. Step 3 (CLINICAL TRANSLATION): 25/68 patients (36.8%) achieved pCR, which appears reasonable for TNBC but lacks a control arm for comparison. Historical pCR rates for chemotherapy alone in TNBC are typically 30-40%, so this result is within expected range but doesn't clearly demonstrate added benefit. Step 4 (POPULATION EFFECTS): No subgroup analyses reported. Step 5 (CONFOUNDERS): Single-arm design prevents definitive efficacy assessment; safety profile shows expected immune-related adverse events consistent with PD-L1 blockade.

failure_modes.evidence: Single-arm study design with no control group makes it impossible to determine if durvalumab added benefit beyond chemotherapy alone. No biomarker data on target engagement or immune activation provided.
